info.name: Backend AI API
info.description:
Generated from the current apps/api NestJS backend. Global prefix is `/api/v1` (except `health`, which is *supposed* to be excluded but isn't — see the note on the Health Check request). Domains: `health-check`, `example` (generic CRUD reference template — real fields are literally `name`/`col1`/`col2`/`col3`), `auth` (real: `POST /auth/register`, `POST /auth/login`), and `student` (real: `GET /students` with status/course/search filters, `POST /students`, `PUT /students/:id` — name is immutable on update, see the Update Student request's description).

Known bug (see CLAUDE.md): both `HealthCheckController` and `ExampleController` use bare `@Controller()` with argument-less `@Get()` handlers, so both resolve to `GET /api/v1`. Because `HealthCheckModule` is imported before `ExampleModule` in `app.module.ts`, the health check handler wins and `ExampleController.getAll` is currently unreachable through the HTTP layer.

Separate known issue: errors thrown inside a domain service (e.g. `auth`'s duplicate-email `ConflictException`) don't go through the documented Express-level `errorHandler` — Nest's own exception pipeline intercepts them first, so the response shape for those is `{statusCode, message}` (2 keys), not the `{status, message, error}` (3 keys) shape the rest of the API uses. Both are shown as example responses on the Register request below.

variable.description: Real Auth0 access token — see the Auth folder description for how to obtain one.
An assignment id — copy one from the List My Assignments response.

item.name: Auth
item.description: Auth0 is the sole identity provider now — register/login/forgot-password/reset-password all happen through Auth0's hosted pages, not this API. Set the {{token}} collection variable to a real Auth0 access token (log into the web app, then copy it from DevTools > Application > Local Storage > the @@auth0spajs@@ key, or from a Network request's Authorization header) before calling any endpoint below — every route requires it except /health.

request.description: Just-in-time provisioning — upserts the local profile row for the authenticated Auth0 user (identified by the verified sub claim on the bearer token). Requires a real Auth0 access token in the {{token}} collection variable; email/firstName/lastName in the body come from the frontend's useAuth0().user after login.

Returns the local profile row for the authenticated user, resolved from the verified sub claim on the bearer token — not from anything in the request. Includes phone, which Auth0 does not hold. 404 if the user has never hit POST /auth/sync (i.e. has never completed a login against this app).

Updates the profile. firstName, lastName and phone are stored only by us; changing email also writes it to Auth0 via the Management API, because Auth0 owns the sign-in identity.

All four fields are required. phone must match the US format (NNN) NNN-NNNN exactly — that is what the frontend PhoneNumberField produces.

An email change fails with 400 for social-login users (google-oauth2|...), since the provider owns their address, and 409 if another profile already uses it. The Auth0 write happens before the local one, so a failure there leaves nothing changed.

Changes the Auth0 password. This app never sees or stores it: the current password is verified by exchanging it with Auth0 (password-realm grant), then the Management API sets the new one.

newPassword must be 8-72 characters and different from currentPassword. Auth0 enforces the tenant policy on top of that and its rejection message is passed through verbatim — so a password can satisfy this API and still be refused as too weak.

400 for social-login users, who have no password here. 401 if currentPassword is wrong.

item.name: Students
item.description:
Real domain — apps/api/src/domains/student. Every field is required on create, matching the frontend Add Student form. `course` is a free-text non-empty string — courses are managed dynamically via the course-management module (frontend mock catalog, no backend endpoint yet), so there's no fixed server-side whitelist to validate against. Deactivate/activate is `PATCH /students/:id/status` (body `{status: 'active'|'deactivated'}`); delete is a soft-delete via `DELETE /students/:id` (sets status to 'deleted', row stays queryable). Both 404 on an id that's already `deleted` — their existence check deliberately excludes deleted students, same as PUT.

Note for List Students / Get Student by ID: these routes only work because StudentModule is registered before ExampleModule in app.module.ts — ExampleController's bare @Controller() + @Get(':id') greedily matches ANY GET /api/v1/<one-segment> path, so it would otherwise swallow the list request first (same root cause as the health/example collision CLAUDE.md documents). Get Student by ID isn't affected by that collision itself (its path has two segments, `/students/:id`), but it depends on the same registration order to reach StudentController at all. If a future domain's route mysteriously 500s with a uuid-cast error, check module registration order before anything else.

query.description: active | deactivated | deleted — defaults to active if omitted
Comma-separated course names, or repeat the param (?course=A&course=B)
Matches first name, last name, or email

request.description: All three query params are optional and independent — combine any subset. Remove the ones you don't need from the Params tab rather than leaving them empty, since an empty search='' still runs (harmlessly matches everything).

item.name: Chat
item.description: Real domain — apps/api/src/domains/chat. WebSocket-backed messaging between admin and a student's record (no separate student-facing client exists in this codebase — "real-time" means every connected admin session sees updates live, not a second party replying). REST is the single write path; the Socket.io gateway at ws(s)://{{baseUrl}}/chat is push-only and broadcasts conversation:started, message:new, conversation:read, and conversation:cleared to all connected clients after each successful write. Attachments are uploaded separately via POST /chat/attachments before being referenced in a Send Message call.

item.name: Courses
item.description: Real domain — apps/api/src/domains/course. Backs the Course Management screen (apps/web/src/modules/course-management) and is the single source of truth the Student Management "Assigned course" dropdown and course filter read from (via their own independent GET /courses calls — no cross-module frontend imports). course on the student table stays a free-text string with no FK to this table. Like the student domain, DELETE /courses/:id is a soft delete (status becomes 'deleted', row stays queryable) — status accepts active/deactivated/deleted for GET, but PATCH .../status only accepts active/deactivated (deleted is DELETE's job, matching updateStudentStatusSchema's same exclusion).

item.name: Assignments
item.description:
Real domain — apps/api/src/domains/assignment. Creating assignments (POST /assignments) and the student's view of them: a table, one assignment, a score, and submitting work. An assignment is either written (text and/or a file, resubmittable) or a quiz (one or more questions — any mix of single choice, multiple choice, short paragraph and long paragraph, with no maximum and no required type or order; one attempt per student).

The four student routes (list, get, score, submit) resolve WHO is asking from the verified token, never from a parameter, so there is no way to request another student's data. A student is the signed-in user whose verified Auth0 email equals an active student's email (checked via Auth0 /userinfo, since users.email is client-supplied and not trusted for this). Anyone else gets 403 — so these requests need a token for a user whose email matches a student row, and that student's course (free-text student.course) must equal a course name that has assignments.

Create Assignment is the exception: it is not student-scoped and has no role check yet. There is no edit or delete endpoint. Use Create Assignment, or run `yarn seed:assignments` in apps/api for sample data, then set the assignmentId collection variable from the id in its response or from List My Assignments.

query.description: todo | submitted | overdue — omit for all. "submitted" includes late work and quizzes pending review.

request.description:
The student's assignment table: every assignment for their course, with a derived state (todo | submitted | late | review | overdue — "review" only for a quiz that has a written question; a quiz of only choice questions is simply "submitted"), the question count (0 for written work) and when they handed it in.

The body is { data: rows[], meta: { page, limit, total, totalPages }, counts: { todo, submitted, overdue } }. counts follow the search but NOT the status filter, so tab badges stay accurate while one tab is selected. Sorted soonest-due first for todo, most recent submission first for submitted, most overdue first for overdue.

The caller must be an enrolled student: their Auth0 email (read from Auth0 /userinfo with this token) must be verified and equal an active student row. Otherwise 403. An invalid status, page or limit is a 400. This is a one-segment GET, so AssignmentModule must stay registered before ExampleModule in app.module.ts.

One assignment: instructions, due date and state, plus — for a quiz — its questions, and the student's own submission or attempt.

Quiz questions carry only id, type (single | multiple | short | descriptive), prompt and options { id, label }. The answer key is never included. quizAttempt.correctAnswers stays null until the quiz's due date has passed.

Set assignmentId from the id in List My Assignments. The caller must be an enrolled student: their Auth0 email (read from Auth0 /userinfo with this token) must be verified and equal an active student row. Otherwise 403. An assignment that belongs to another course is a 404 (not 403) so ids can't be probed; a malformed id is a 400.

The student's score. For a quiz: choiceScore { correct, total, percentage } (choice questions only), reviewStatus, and a per-question breakdown { questionId, isCorrect, correctOptionIds } that is null until the due date has passed. For written work there is no score: choiceScore is null and reviewStatus is "pending".

Written answers (short and long paragraph) are marked by hand, so they are not part of choiceScore. reviewStatus is "pending" while a quiz has written answers waiting to be read, and "graded" for a quiz of only choice questions — there is nothing for a person to mark. 404 if the student has not submitted yet. The caller must be an enrolled student: their Auth0 email (read from Auth0 /userinfo with this token) must be verified and equal an active student row. Otherwise 403.

formdata.description: Up to 5000 characters. Optional if a file is attached.
Optional. pdf, doc, docx, png, jpg or jpeg, up to 10 MB.

request.description:
Hands in a WRITTEN assignment as multipart/form-data — send answerText, a file, or both. Resubmitting replaces the previous submission entirely, including its file (a resubmission without a file clears it). Past the due date it is still accepted but flagged late.

Returns 201 with the updated assignment (same shape as Get Assignment). Neither field → 400; wrong file type or over 10 MB → 400. The stored file name on disk is never exposed, and uploads are private — there is no public route to them. Sending this to a quiz is a 400 (use Submit Quiz). The caller must be an enrolled student: their Auth0 email (read from Auth0 /userinfo with this token) must be verified and equal an active student row. Otherwise 403.

Submits a QUIZ as JSON. choices maps a question id to the option ids picked; texts maps a short or long paragraph question's id to the written answer (max 3000 characters). The ids above are placeholders — replace them with the real question and option ids from Get Assignment, or the answers are ignored.

ONE ATTEMPT ONLY: a second submit is a 409, enforced by a database constraint so simultaneous requests cannot both succeed. Marking happens on the server and multi-answer questions are all-or-nothing (the chosen set must match exactly). Unanswered questions are allowed. A key that is not a UUID is a 400 rather than being dropped, so a malformed payload cannot burn the attempt. A file attachment on a quiz is a 400.

Returns 201 with the updated assignment; use Get Assignment Score for the marks. The caller must be an enrolled student: their Auth0 email (read from Auth0 /userinfo with this token) must be verified and equal an active student row. Otherwise 403.

Creates an assignment — the builder's "Publish" action. Send kind ("quiz", the default, or "written"), title, courseId, instructions, dueAt (ISO timestamp, must be in the future) and questions. Set the courseId collection variable to the id of an ACTIVE course first (GET /courses), and change dueAt if 2030-12-31 has passed.

A quiz needs at least ONE question — there is no minimum above that, no maximum, and no required question type or order. Each question is single (radio), multiple (checkboxes), short (one-line written answer) or descriptive (long written answer). Single and multiple need 2-5 options and a valid answer key via isCorrect: exactly one correct for single, at least one for multiple. short and descriptive take no options — any sent are dropped. A written assignment has no questions (a non-empty list is a 400).

Returns 201 with the new assignment, its questions and options WITH the answer key (isCorrect) — it goes to the person who just wrote it; students never receive it before the quiz's due date. Copy data.id into the assignmentId variable to use the other requests in this folder. The assignment, its questions and its options are saved in one transaction, so a failure leaves nothing half-created.

400 for a missing or empty field, a title over 255 or a question over 500 characters, a past dueAt, an unknown kind or question type, or a choice question with a bad answer key (the message names the question, e.g. "Question 2: mark the correct answer."). 404 if the course does not exist; 400 "Choose an active course." if it is deactivated or deleted.

NOT tied to a student, so unlike the other requests here the caller does not need to match a student record. There is also no role check yet: ANY signed-in user can create an assignment until the app has roles. Errors use Nest's { statusCode, message } shape, with several problems joined by semicolons.

Intended route is GET /health (see main.ts's `exclude: ['health']` and startup log line), but the exclude never matches because HealthCheckController's computed path is '' not 'health'. With the global prefix applied it actually lands on GET /api/v1, same as ExampleController.getAll — this request hits the real, currently-working path.
Kept here so this collection stops 404ing the moment the routing bug in CLAUDE.md's 'Known pre-existing bugs' section is fixed — delete once that lands.
Only mounted when NODE_ENV !== 'production' (see main.ts).
